llm.summary: The SKILL.md describes a plausible local-first security plugin, but the skill package metadata and the fact that this is instruction-only (it directs you to install external code and to register with a remote service) create inconsistencies and risk that should be reviewed before installing.

dimensions.detail: The README-like SKILL.md claims a runtime security plugin that hooks agent events and performs local sanitization — which is coherent with installing an external OpenGuardrails package. However the registry metadata (slug 'moltguard', owner id, source/homepage unknown) does not match the GitHub URLs embedded in SKILL.md, creating an attribution mismatch that deserves verification.

dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: Instructions are mostly installation and activation steps and descriptions of what the external plugin will do; they do not ask the agent to read unrelated system files or exfiltrate secrets. They do instruct a registration flow that performs network POSTs and writes credentials to ~/.openclaw/credentials/openguardrails/credentials.json — which is expected for a cloud-opt-in feature but should be validated before use.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: There is no built-in install spec in the skill bundle (instruction-only). SKILL.md tells you to install from npm or clone GitHub and then run the plugin — those are standard, but they mean you will execute external code from npm/GitHub. The skill claims 'no install-time network calls' for the plugin itself, but following the install instructions necessarily pulls code over the network; verify the package/repo before installing.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill declares no required environment variables or credentials. The only persistent credential action described is registration which stores credentials locally (~/.openclaw/credentials/openguardrails/credentials.json) and may associate your email/agent ID with a remote service — this is proportional for an opt-in cloud assessment feature but should be confirmed.

dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always:false and default autonomous invocation are normal. The activation step writes credentials to a user-local path; that is expected for a cloud opt-in. Because the SKILL.md itself is instruction-only, the runtime hooks and persistence will come from the external plugin you are asked to install — audit that code before giving it persistent presence.

llm.guidance: This skill describes a legitimate-sounding security plugin but is instruction-only and tells you to install and run external code from npm/GitHub and to register with a remote service. Before installing: 1) Verify the upstream repository and npm package (author, repo name, commit history, release tags) actually match the URLs in SKILL.md and are trustworthy; the registry metadata here (slug 'moltguard' / unknown source) does not match the SKILL.md’s GitHub links and should be reconciled. 2) Audit the repository files the README points to (sanitizer, detector, index.ts) to confirm no unexpected network calls or secrets handling. 3) Understand what data the registration will send and what credentials will be stored in ~/.openclaw/credentials/openguardrails/credentials.json; consider using a disposable account or container if you want to test. 4) Prefer installing from a verified GitHub release or an officially published npm package (check checksums/signatures) rather than a random commit. If you cannot verify the upstream authorship or code, treat this skill as potentially risky and avoid installing it in production environments.
